goal: Scaffold squeeze v0.1: intuitive one-command build/run wrapper around crush-pkg's PackageBuilder
summary: Session start: Scaffold squeeze v0.1: intuitive one-command build/run wrapper around crush-pkg's PackageBuilder

decision_title: squeeze: new peer repo wrapping crush-pkg, named after crush's juice/pressing metaphor
decision_reason: crush-pkg build and crush-pkg run are two separate, uncomposed steps today — run interprets the entry source directly via CapsuleRunner/PayloadFormat detection, it never calls build() or writes target/. squeeze's whole value in v0.1 is composing check->build->write target/->run into one command with one status line per stage, the way 'cargo run' does, without reimplementing any of crush-pkg's actual compile/run pipeline (PackageBuilder is the real work; squeeze is a thin composition layer).
summary: Decision: squeeze: new peer repo wrapping crush-pkg, named after crush's juice/pressing metaphor

rejected_alternatives.reason: heavily conflicted name — BobBuildTool/bob (embedded/bitbake-style), benchkram/bob (multi-language monorepo build tool, conceptually near-identical to this), bobbin-cli (embedded Rust deploy), a published 'bob' crate on crates.io. Confirmed via web search before naming.

would inherit the same feature-unification headaches CRUSHAST-WEB-1 (crush-web) just spent real effort untangling, and squeeze is meant to grow into an ecosystem-wide tool (potentially touching buckets/crush-web/exo-light later), not something crush-ast-workspace-scoped. Standalone peer repo matches the established pattern for new ecosystem tools this session (buckets, interactd, crush-vscode).

outcome: v0.1 skeleton: squeeze (default: check+build+run in one flow) / new / check / build / run subcommands, thin wrapper over crush_pkg::builder::PackageBuilder + crush_vm::run_with_caps. Verified end-to-end against a real 'squeeze new demo' -> target/demo.cvm + demo.casm.json -> 'hello from Crush' output, both via the default flow and via 'squeeze run' with no prior build.

summary: v0.1 skeleton verified working: new/check/build/run + default composed flow, backed by crush-pkg::PackageBuilder (peer path-dep to ../crush-ast). No CI, no tests yet. Not published to crates.io/GitHub yet — nixpt/squeeze repository URL in Cargo.toml is aspirational.

squeeze v0.1 scaffolded and verified: check/build/run/new subcommands + default one-shot flow, all thin wrappers over crush_pkg::builder::PackageBuilder. Only language="crush" capsules are wired; Script/Native intentionally out of scope for v0.1 (see main.rs module doc).
next: Add tests (crush-pkg's own test suite is the model: tempdir + scaffold_package + assert on target/ output)
Wire Script/Native capsule support via crush_pkg::runners::{CapsuleRunner, CrushRunner} instead of the PackageBuilder-only path
Decide on real GitHub remote (nixpt/squeeze) and push, or fold into an existing org — repo is currently local-only
Consider: crush-web's new run_blob(bytes) could let 'squeeze build' target wasm32 output too — natural next integration point between the two things built this session
